structured_output.summary: RED is genuinely causal and GREEN implements the frozen carrier design correctly: the record binds protocol/object/genesis/author/closed+successor epoch and anchors/Cut/QC/snapshot/prior-digest/prior+new boundary/lineage under the creator finality key; the opener re-verifies against an independently authenticated floor; the signing request is one-use and type-segregated; derivation is bounded by maxEpochVertices with exact issued/outbox equality, dense-lineage equality and graph membership; the Node-private wrapper is the sole normalization seam for exactly one stage and four verify consumers, authenticates before stripping, and restores only the opened successor pair; registry-v1.json, its wire table, v3-live.ts, dependencies, thresholds, and the protocol-v3 root export roster are untouched. Two blocking gaps remain. First, the frozen derivation admits a permanently unrecoverable close failure for a state that is reachable on the ordinary product path (a durably committed issued row whose journal/graph append fails), which the plan's own stop rule says must be resliced to the issuance-outcome owner rather than absorbed here. Second, the adversarial GREEN row set the accepted plan froze is largely unexecuted: the entire creator-close derivation fail-closed branch family has no test anywhere in the repository.

findings.title: Orphaned issued row permanently blocks every later creator close
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:396-407 requires every scanned row above the prior boundary to satisfy `decoded.anchor === input.currentTrust.currentAnchorDigest` and `decoded.epoch === input.currentTrust.currentEpoch`, else it throws CREATOR_ISSUANCE_RETIREMENT_UNAVAILABLE. packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:5674 commits the durable issued/outbox pair via `transactIssue` BEFORE the journal append (5765-5783) and graph append (5793-5799); every post-commit failure there returns `committedFailure(...)` (journal-rejected, graph-rejected, admission-rejected, authorization-rejected), leaving a durably issued row that is absent from both the journal and the close graph. The D.110c-0c1 architecture audit recorded in the plan states no product path invokes `prunePublishedPrefix()`, so no product path can ever remove that row.
findings.impact: Sequence: at epoch 0 the orphan is the unadmitted suffix, `truncated` is set, the boundary stops below it and the 0->1 close succeeds (the plan's 'fail-safe suffix'). At the 1->2 close the orphan is the first row past `afterKey`, still carries the epoch-0 epoch and anchor, and fails the anchor/epoch equality at creator-close.ts:400-402. Every subsequent close throws the same token. The room can never advance an epoch again and there is no recovery, prune, or repair path. Before this change the orphan row was inert, so this is a new unrecoverable liveness regression on exactly the repeated-epoch golden path D.110c-c/d must reach.
findings.required_action: Do not weaken the dense frontier. Apply the plan's own stop rule at production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:95770-95775 by recording that the permanent-hole state is demonstrated reachable on the product path from the post-commit failure window in `issueOneVertex`, and assigning a bounded issuance-outcome repair/quarantine owner (D.110c-0c1 or D.110c-c) as a named blocking prerequisite. Correct the plan sentence 'An issued-but-unadmitted suffix may remain fail-safe above the boundary' to state explicitly that such a suffix freezes all later closes.

findings.title: Frozen adversarial GREEN rows for the derivation path are unexecuted
findings.evidence: The accepted plan (production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:95914-95924) froze adversarial GREEN rows including duplicate/gapped issued address, issued/outbox substitution, issued-but-unadmitted suffix, admitted row after a gap, graph/replay omission, post-capture mutation, ambiguous persistence, empty initialization, exhausted-lineage single refusal, and pending-floor stable/candidate selection. The only 0c1a test file is tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1a-retirement-checkpoint-red.test.ts (2 tests); it exercises only carrier open/recreate, field/signature/size mutants, closure-delta mutants, signing-request one-use and cross-type refusal, epoch-1 same-boundary replacement, and a stale-prior fork. It never mutates the issuance store, close graph, or lineage. A repository-wide search shows `D110C_0C1A_RETIREMENT_CHECKPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` appears in tests only as the RED token constant at tests/fixtures/phase-6b-d110c-0c1a/retirement-checkpoint-contract.ts:17, and that RED branch is now dead because the fixture yields one carrier. No test asserts any refusal from the production derivation.
findings.impact: The thirteen fail-closed refusal sites in `issuanceRetirementCandidate()` (packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:318, 336, 340, 351, 358, 382, 388, 391, 406, 409, 414, 427, 436) are the entire authority that D.110c-0c1 will use to hide old issuance rows, and none of them is verified by an executable gate. A regression that silently widens the admitted frontier (a paging off-by-one, a dropped graph-membership check, a relaxed dense-lineage equality) would pass every current suite and hand D.110c-0c1 a boundary that authorizes hiding unadmitted or substituted rows. The unexecuted 'issued-but-unadmitted suffix' and 'admitted row after a gap' rows are also precisely the rows that would have surfaced the P1 above.
findings.required_action: Before closing D.110c-0c1a, add one focused derivation-adversarial test file over the existing genuine fixture that drives the store/graph seams and asserts CREATOR_ISSUANCE_RETIREMENT_UNAVAILABLE for at minimum: gapped address, duplicate address, issued/outbox substitution, graph omission followed by an in-graph row, incomplete lineage (`lineage.next` mismatch), exhausted lineage, over-limit scan, and empty epoch-0 initialization. Alternatively, if any row is judged out of scope, record it explicitly in the plan as a deferred row with a named owner rather than leaving the frozen list silently unmet.

findings.title: Epoch-0 carrier author is unbound outside creator-close
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:175-180 accepts an epoch-0 initialization carrier after checking only `priorAdmittedAuthorSequence === null` and the genesis sentinel; it never constrains `identity.author`. Author continuity is enforced only from epoch 1 onward at creator-transition-advance.ts:196 (`openedProposed.identity.author === openedCurrent.identity.author`). The only binding to a real issuance author is in the minting path at packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:350 (`identity.author !== input.issuanceScope.author`), which the four verify consumers do not reach.
findings.impact: A durable epoch-0 carrier signed by the genuine creator key over the genuine Cut/QC/snapshot/anchors but naming a different `author` would be accepted by all four verify consumers. Residual risk is low today because creator-close always sets `author` from the live issuance scope and the design is creator-only single-author, but D.110c-0c1 will derive per-author hiding authority from this field.
findings.required_action: Disposition only: record in the D.110c-0c1 owner text that the consumer must compare the opened carrier's `author` against its independently resolved issuance scope before using the boundary to classify any row, since the transition wrapper does not establish that binding at epoch 0.
